steps.title: Start the tomato base
steps.instruction: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium. Cook onion with a pinch of salt until soft and translucent, 6–8 minutes. Add garlic and basil; stir 45 seconds until fragrant. Add tomatoes with their juice and broth. Bring to a simmer.

steps.title: Simmer and blend smooth
steps.instruction: Simmer uncovered 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the soup thickens slightly and raw onion flavor is gone. Blend with an immersion blender until completely smooth — or cool slightly and blend in batches if using a countertop blender. Return to the pot, stir in cream, and season with salt and pepper. Hold at a bare simmer (do not boil cream).

steps.title: Make grilled cheese croutons
steps.instruction: Butter one side of each bread slice. Flip dry sides up and cover with cheddar. Pair slices into sandwiches and press in a skillet over medium-low with a spatula weight until deeply golden and cheese melts, about 4 minutes per side. Transfer to a cutting board.

steps.title: Cube the melts and finish soup
steps.instruction: Cut grilled cheese sandwiches into ¾-inch cubes — these are your croutons, not raw bread. Ladle hot soup into bowls and float a handful of cheesy croutons on top. Serve extra croutons in a warm pan at the line so they stay crisp.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Keep the pot on low simmer on the stove — ladle from the side so the bottom doesn't scorch.
Set shredded cheese, crackers, and hot sauce in a row beside the pot.
Line up Tomato Soup with Grilled Cheese Croutons on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Creamy tomato soup topped with real grilled-cheese cubes. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Ground turkey swaps 1:1 for beef in chili if the crew wants leaner.
